our model is the first to demonstrate a progressive module architecture that learns a set of tasks progressively, without suffering from catastrophic forgetting, while also learning a more human-like and interpretable reasoning process.
our model is a novel neural network architecture for learning to reason, that can learn progressively, is fully differentiable and can be trained end to end.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a model for learning to solve visual reasoning tasks that is both effective and interpretable, and is trained in an end-to-end manner.
we are proposing a new neural architecture for learning tasks in a progressive manner, and show how it can be applied in a visual reasoning setting.
we are able to learn a set of tasks progressively by building on top existing modules and their solutions, without suffering from forgetting, and with better interpretability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability to compose solutions to subtasks in an incremental way is an important component for learning complex tasks.
we can use neural networks to learn to solve complex tasks by building on top existing skills, in a way that resembles human learning.
a progressive approach to learning can lead to better generalization and interpretability.
